title: Fix #40's false evidence claim, make its post-merge duty executable, and measure its layout
body:
## What was wrong

#40 shipped a dashboard whose top-line claim was false, a post-merge duty that could not be executed or verified, and a figure whose layout was asserted rather than measured. Eleven findings (C3–C5, M1–M10) plus six minor ones; all are addressed here. **Nothing was merged, closed, commented on, or pushed over #40** — this branch stacks on its head.

## Changes, by finding

**C3 — "evidence: 35/35" was a false claim.** It was computed as `milestones_with_evidence`, which counted a roadmap path *reference* as an evidence record. The census is now split in both the figure and the README: `milestones_with_evidence` 19/35, `milestones_with_filed_record` **0/35**, and a citation is not counted as a record (`filed = [e for e in evidence if e.split("#")[0].startswith("docs/evidence/")]`). Six labels were reworded so "on file" now means filed, not cited. A `docs/`-prefix variant was rejected on purpose: it would count `docs/ACCEPTANCE.md` as filed evidence.

**C4 — the duty was unexecutable and unverifiable.** `post-merge` read `check && docs-check && dashboard-reconcile --here`, where `--here` reported **CURRENT** against any branch — `main` included — because the reconciler asked which branch was checked out instead of where the change landed. Now `post-merge` regenerates, verifies, and records; `dashboard-reconcile` resolves its target as `origin/main` (falling back to `origin/HEAD`); and verification is a committed machine-readable receipt, `docs/evidence/dashboard-reconciliation.json`, read **from the target** via `git show`, not inferred from a commit message. `AGENTS.md` was re-titled and re-explained: this is a standing responsibility you discharge, not a monitor you install — there are no check-runs, no workflows, and no protection rule to do it for you.

**C5 — the banner is 2400×250 and the matrix 1200×1200.** `make presentation` rewrites `pc5-banner.svg` as a side effect, and the matrix grows every time a status changes. `docs/PRESENTATION.md` §5 now says plainly that both are regenerated in place, that `ci/build.yml` is a definition in the tree while `.github/workflows/` does not exist, and that nothing currently enforces drift.

**M1 — the level ladder was painted green by layout, not by data.** `status_grid` hardcoded `fill=GREEN`. It now derives from `info["complete"]`, and `tests/test_progress_matrix.py` reads the committed `<rect>`/`<text>` of the figure and fails if any verified cell sits above L2.

**M2 — 12px leading against 11px text, and 7–8 lines clipped.** `LEAD` is 15px in `fit_lines` and both note slots accept up to 7 lines; the footer's line spacing was 8px and is 13px; the canvas grows 1200→1223, so the footnote is visible again.

**M3 — "all 39 evidence paths resolve" was the only number with no test.** The census is now computed in `tests/test_progress_matrix.py` from `docs/ROADMAP.md` independently of the generator and compared against the figure, README and `claims.json`.

**M4 — text drawn over text.** `region_head` budgets the right-hand figure by measuring it and clips only the title; `collisions()` groups labels by baseline using the same `measure()`; a test asserts **no `…` appears anywhere in the committed figure**, so the fix is measured layout, not suppressed ellipsis.

**M5 — `tools/presentation.py` is 1700+ lines.** Left as-is deliberately: extracting a layout engine would move code the finding is about without making it verifiable. The four words are separated instead (M10): *cited / filed / checked / reconciled* now name different things in the figure, README, `claims.json` and glossary.

**M6 — `milestone_count` counted all 39 status rows; `validate()` recomputed an estimate.** Both take the authoritative number; `milestones_cited` is the field's real meaning.

**M7 — `test_layout_within_panel` asserted constants against constants.** Replaced by tests that parse the committed SVG's geometry, and the guards are now *falsifiable*: a doctored ladder, a figure with a real overlap, a heading whose title is 22 characters too long, and a roadmap citing a missing path each make the suite fail. Two more close gaps a mutation battery found: `check()` must refuse a **current but colliding** figure (byte-equality alone cannot see a layout defect), and `overflow()` may not keep its own width estimate.

**M8 — `dashboard-reconcile` never read the roadmap.** Every range commit is now classified by the *state names* it touches (`in progress` → in_progress; `unblocked`/`blocked`/`not started` also matched), and **a commit that touches no tracked state is reported, not hidden**.

**M9 — "CI enforces regeneration" was already written into AGENTS.md.** The claim is gone; the six-step procedure, the exit-code table, the receipt contract and the explicit "never merge" are in its place.

**M10 — `reconciled` overloaded with `checked`.** `claims.json` distinguishes `checked` (a gate passed) from `reconciled` (a receipt recorded); the glossary carries `boundary`, `citation`, `CURRENT`, `filed`, `OUTSTANDING`, `receipt`, `reconciliation`.

**m1–m6** — `git()` raises instead of returning `""`; a shallow clone is an ERROR; a `^0`-suffixed remote HEAD resolves; missing/malformed/foreign/future-naming/incomplete receipts fail closed; `--target` cannot point at a *commit*; the `Makefile` got a `.PHONY` entry, and `--check` was deleted from the reconciler because `presentation-check` already checks.

## Behaviour you can reproduce

```
$ make presentation-check      0   7 figures and 6 blocks current, 13 status rows match roadmap
$ make docs-check              0   68 Markdown files, 36 make targets, 229 internal links resolve
$ python3 tools/dashboard_reconcile.py            # on a branch with no receipt on main
1   NO RECONCILIATION RECEIPT on origin/main … run:
      python3 tools/dashboard_reconcile.py --bootstrap --inspect <full SHA of the commit being reconciled>
$ python3 tools/dashboard_reconcile.py --bootstrap --inspect <sha>   # gate red on a bare clone
2   ERROR — the gates must pass before a reconciliation is recorded … (exit 2, never 0)
```

Exit codes: **0 CURRENT** (an empty range still enumerates the output and proves the receipt is current), **1 OUTSTANDING** (a `tools/**` or `docs/**` commit on the target, a docs-only merge, a root file with no figure effect, a malformed receipt, a receipt naming a commit that is not on the target, a dirty source), **2 ERROR** (shallow clone, `origin/main` unresolvable, gates red at record time, dirty generated output). The receipt is read from the target so recording cannot be faked with an uncommitted file; `--record` refuses when source is uncommitted and the generator refuses when generated output is. `--here` remains an explicitly-scoped diagnostic; `--allow-shallow` was **not** kept, because a reconciler that accepts a grafted history would be accepting a knowingly-incomplete range.

## Tests

Measured by running each command and keeping its exit code: `make check` at `2cdbc9f`, the three suites and both checks re-run on the tree carrying this entry, the only difference between them being this document (gate: `docs-check`, exit 0). Three scenarios were wrong and rewritten: s31 (a squash mints a SHA that no longer exists in the rewritten history), s16/s17 (a git identity was missing, so `commit_tree` failed rather than the tool misbehaving). `tests/test_dashboard_reconcile.py` carries 45 scenarios including 22 built after the fixes for the audit's own defects, and 4 for the merge-content rule: a PR merge that delivers a reconciliation clears the moment it lands because every commit it introduces is reviewed, while one unreviewed commit inside re-opens it by SHA, and a squash still has to be recorded — the honest difference between the two strategies, not an accident of history-walking.

| suite | tests | result |
|---|---|---|
| `tests.test_dashboard_reconcile` | 46 | OK (skipped=1: one scenario needs a system GitLab CLI) |
| `tests.test_progress_matrix` | 56 | OK |
| `tests.test_presentation` | 66 | OK |
| `make check` (`unit psm docs-check citations-check presentation-check brand-check`) | 1037 tests | **exit 0**, `OK (skipped=110)` |

Diff against #40's head `8e3f0b6`: 13 files changed, 2928 insertions(+), 320 deletions(-), across 9 commits — `c158ef2` the reconciler and its scenarios, `a29df65` the measured layout and the figure's regression tests, `76253f5` the documentation, `4b56a65` the merge-content rule plus the three guard tests that the mutation battery proved were missing, and `96d0b9d`…`5bc5d5d` the correction record in `docs/TEST_RESULTS.md` §28–§29 (three small commits, because two of them fixed numbers the first one got wrong).

## Measured presentation state (this is what the audit could not claim)

`inspect_svg.py` (independent of `tools/`) on the regenerated matrix: **335/335 `<text>` nodes and 195/195 `<rect>` nodes accounted for, 0 overflow, 0 collisions, 0 truncations**, every region inside its frame, all 7 SVGs well-formed. Fill census: 56 green (50 of them inside the "one green row per verified level" legend chip, 6 in the ladder: 4+1+0+0+0+1, exactly matching `2/6`), 11 cyan, 88 cell grey, 23 dark, 16 amber. Rasterized at 2× (2400×2446): no ink outside the artwork rect, no clipped glyph.

## Negative controls

A mutation battery run from outside the repository — the harness is **not committed**: it copies the tree to a scratch directory, swaps one statement, and re-runs the suite. **34 control attempts in three rounds: 24 caught**, 5 needles failed to match after the code moved and 1 produced unparseable source (harness faults, reported as faults), and **3 controls were genuinely missed** — which is the result that mattered. It also caught the harness itself: run twice against an uncommitted tree it reported 0/6, because the copy is reset with `git checkout -- .`, reverting the very tests under test; from then on it only runs on commits. Caught include: disk-skipping evidence census, `fill=GREEN` in the ladder, the measured-heading rule removed, `fit` never truncating, a missing receipt reported as clean, a future-naming receipt, `verify()` ignored, wholesale README exemption, `--target` accepting the checked-out branch, `git()` swallowing failure, a shallow record, a source-dirty record, an exempt-anything-a-merge-touches rule, and the three guards under M7. Three round-two controls *were* missed and that was the useful result: they showed collisions and overflow were asserted only through helper calls, and that an empty range could be produced by swallowing an error — all three now have tests, and each re-run caught. One final needle failed to patch (a cosmetic report string), so it is not counted as a pass; that message is asserted in scenario 37 by exact substring.

## Two decisions worth challenging

1. **A merge is exempt on content, not on existence.** Exempting merges as such lets any merge self-approve; requiring the merge SHA to be named makes the duty re-open forever. The rule "every commit the merge introduces is named or is generated output" is the only one I found that closes both. Its consequence: after a *squash* you still run `make post-merge` once.
2. **`tests/test_presentation.py` couples README links to a tmp-dir symlink list.** A fixture that symlinks `CONTRIBUTING.md` but not `AGENTS.md` made `check()` report `link target missing` for a perfectly valid README. The reconciler's README exemption was fixed by *removing* a link that pointed at a file the fixture never had, rather than by editing the fixture list or weakening the test.

## What remains unverified

* The absence of CI: **0 check-runs and 0 workflow files** on #40, confirmed live with `gh api repos/SpicyBadran/PC5/commits/8e3f0b6/check-runs` and `contents/.github/workflows` (404).
* Branch protection: `GET /repos/SpicyBadran/PC5/branches/main/protection` returns **403** with this token — it may be set; I cannot read it.
* The author's local clone and their `origin/main`: not observable from here; nothing in this PR assumes `HEAD` or `origin/main` equals `8e3f0b6`/`52f682c`, and the reconciler resolves refs at run time.
* #41 and #42 do not exist on the remote (404), so the earlier plan's premise was corrected to: stack on #40's head, do not merge, do not push `main`.
* **The receipt cannot be recorded by this PR.** It is recorded on the target, so the first one has to be bootstrapped on `main` after a merge; until then `make post-merge` verifies and records, and a bare clone's `--record` fails at the gates by design.
* Deliberately **not** done: no edit to any file under the original `/home/user/pc5` workspace (it stays byte-identical), and no merge of #40.

## Follow-ups worth their own PR

* Bootstrap the receipt on `main` (`--bootstrap --inspect <the merge sha>`) in the same commit as the regenerated figures, so the next `post-merge` starts from a real boundary.
* Add `.github/workflows/ci.yml` running `make check` plus `presentation-check` and `docs-check`; until then the sentence "CI enforces regeneration" stays out of every document.
* Give `docs/ROADMAP.md` real filed records — the census will honestly read `0/35` until something exists under `docs/evidence/`, which is the point of separating citation from filing.
* `docs/TEST_RESULTS.md` §28 recorded a suite count (968) that was stale by the time it was committed. §29 corrects it in the append-only style this repository uses; a header explaining that convention, so future entries are measured before commit, is still worth its own change.
